headlines.text: Looking back to 2025, when there was a changing of the guard for the AEW International Title as Kenny Omega vs. Konosuke Takeshita battled it out, appearing on Revolution, rated 8.95 ? a war that left everything in the ring ? ending the champion's reign at 5 defenses. It was the 50th time the AEW International Title had been on the line, a genuinely rare milestone for that title. Making his AEW pay-per-view return after a lengthy illness layoff, Omega countered a One Winged Angel escape into a crucifix pin to dethrone Takeshita for the International Championship.

Rewind to 2022, when the AEW TNT Title had a new owner by the end of the night as Scorpio Sky vs. Sammy Guevara battled it out, appearing on Dynamite, rated 5.59 ? ending the champion's reign at 5 defenses. Guevara's taped ribs finally gave out under the pressure of real outside interference ? Dan Lambert and Ethan Page's involvement, evened out by Tay Conti, ultimately let Sky capture his first singles title in AEW.

2024 brought us this moment: Jarrett & Lethal & Briscoe announced their arrival in style, headlining their very first AEW appearance as a team in an Atlanta Street Fight match, appearing on Collision, rated 6.84.

secondaries.text: 2025 brought us this moment: Toni Storm vs. Mariah May fought tooth and nail for the AEW Women's World Title in a Hollywood Ending match, appearing on Revolution, rated 9.48 ? an all-timer. Mariah May was chasing gold for the 10th time. In a "Hollywood Ending" Falls Count Anywhere match soaked in blood, Storm put May through a table with a Code Zero before retaining her Women's Title with a Storm Zero.

Rewind to 2025, when Will Ospreay vs. Kyle Fletcher settled things in a Steel Cage match on Revolution, rated 9.43 ? a five-star epic, on an outstanding Revolution '25 show that earned an overall rating of 8.84. In their first-ever steel cage match, Ospreay busted Fletcher open with a screwdriver before finishing him with a Tiger Driver '91 in a bloody, weapons-filled war.

Back on this day in 2025, Swerve Strickland vs. Ricochet met in a Number One Contender on Revolution, rated 8.56 ? a match fans still talk about, on an outstanding Revolution '25 show that earned an overall rating of 8.84.
